name: Covered call writing
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Earning Equity Option Premium
caseLead: The investment case rests on the tendency of call options on shares and stock indices to be priced above the volatility that the market ultimately delivers, so call sellers collect a premium on top of the dividend yield. The premium persists because investors pay for upside and protection, and geopolitical and policy uncertainty keep demand for options strong even in years when the market moves little.
caseRest: The main risk is that the strategy keeps most of the fall in share prices but gives up most of the gain in strong rallies. The premium collected covers only a small part of a large sell-off, as in March 2020 when shares fell about 34% in five weeks. Rebounds after sell-offs also cap returns, because calls sold at lower prices are exercised when the market recovers.
figNote: The large figure on each card shows the highest closing level of the VIX during the episode. The VIX measures the volatility that S&P 500 options price in for the next 30 days: it has averaged about 19 over the long run, while readings above 30 signal market stress.

events.title: Bank failures send equities sharply lower
events.text: The Lehman Brothers collapse lifted the VIX to an 80 close in October 2008, and the S&P 500 fell about 17% over the month. The strategy lost because the call premium covered only a small part of the fall in the shares.

events.title: US downgrade lifts implied volatility sharply
events.text: The US credit rating downgrade and the euro area debt crisis lifted the VIX to a 48 close in August 2011. Results were mixed because high implied volatility raised call premiums, but the shares fell and the strategy gave up part of that income.

events.title: Brexit vote causes a brief equity sell-off
events.text: The United Kingdom vote to leave the European Union lifted the VIX to a 26 close in June 2016, and the S&P 500 recovered its losses within two weeks. The strategy gained because the elevated premium was collected while the shares regained their value.

events.title: Covid sell-off overwhelms call premium
events.text: The VIX reached an 83 close in March 2020 as the S&P 500 fell about 34% in five weeks. The strategy lost heavily because the call premium covered only a small part of the fall.

events.title: Yen carry unwind creates rich option premium
events.text: A Bank of Japan rate rise and weak US jobs data unwound yen-funded positions, lifting the VIX to a 39 close in August 2024 before it fell back. The strategy gained because the higher call premium was collected while the S&P 500 recovered within weeks.

events.title: US tariffs lift option premium and cut shares
events.text: Sweeping US tariffs lifted the VIX to a 52 close in April 2025 and cut the S&P 500 about 19% from its February high. Results were mixed because the premium cushioned the fall, but the calls capped the sharp rebound that followed.

instrument: S&P 500 shares held through an ETF, with one-month call options; rolled monthly
rules: Calls sold 3% to 5% above the share price when implied volatility exceeds realised volatility; call size reduced when the VIX is below 14; calls bought back if the index rises through the strike before expiry
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads and commissions deducted at each roll
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from option premium to downside protection

legs.position: Put options, 3 months, 10% out of the money
legs.purpose: Limits losses in a large sell-off
Holds cash for rebalancing and earns the cash rate

entry: Calls sold when implied volatility is at least 2 points above realised volatility
size: Calls written on 80% to 100% of shares held
exit: Calls bought back at 70% of premium collected, or 5 days before expiry
stop: Call writing paused and share weight cut by a third if the index falls 15% from its high
marketWatch: Rehyn monitors the gap between one-month implied and realised volatility on the S&P 500, the slope of the volatility surface and the dividend yield, because they set the premium available. Scheduled central bank meetings, tariff announcements and earnings seasons are the events that most often change option prices. A sharp rally would cap returns, while a sustained fall would test how much the premium can cushion.

favourable.heading: Range-bound equity markets
favourable.text: Sideways markets favour the strategy because the calls expire worthless and the premium adds to dividends without capping any gain. In 2015 the S&P 500 was almost flat, and covered call indices outperformed it.

favourable.heading: Elevated implied volatility
favourable.text: High implied volatility favours the strategy because call premiums rise while the shares often stabilise, so the income collected is larger. After the August 2024 volatility spike, the VIX returned below 20 within two weeks and the larger premium was kept.

favourable.heading: Short-lived equity sell-offs
favourable.text: Short-lived falls favour the strategy because the call premium offsets part of the fall and the shares recover before the calls are exercised. After the June 2016 Brexit vote the S&P 500 regained its losses within two weeks, so the strategy kept the premium.

adverse.heading: Deep equity sell-offs
adverse.text: Large falls hurt the strategy because the premium collected is small compared with the loss on the shares, and the calls give no protection below the premium received. In March 2020 the S&P 500 fell about 34% in five weeks, far more than the call premium could offset.

adverse.heading: Sharp rallies after a sell-off
adverse.text: Strong rebounds hurt the strategy because the calls cap the gain at the strike price while the shares continue to rise. After the March 2020 low the S&P 500 rose about 40% in three months, and a covered call portfolio captured only part of the rise.

adverse.heading: Rising rates and inflation
adverse.text: Rising rates hurt the strategy because they lower share valuations, and the premium does not offset a persistent fall, so losses build slowly. In 2022 the S&P 500 fell about 18% and a covered call index fell about 11%, which shows that the cushion was only partial.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in the S&P 500 and implied volatility, which are then applied to the share holdings and the call options currently written, including the cap on gains.
altTitle: Where Else Can Investors Find Option Income?

related.why: Sells index options without owning the shares. Bears crash risk, with large losses when volatility spikes.
Earns dividends from companies with covered payouts. Bears equity price risk and dividend cuts, with no cap on gains.
related.cue: Equity income without a cap on gains

related.why: Buys index options that pay out in a crash. Bears the premium cost, paying in calm years.
related.cue: Provides the protection this strategy lacks
